summary: End-to-end testing of the new Pupu Admin dashboard (auth + overview + server detail + control + protected route + logout + public status regression). Backend: 13/13 pytest cases passed against public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Frontend: full Playwright flow passed — /admin without token redirects to /admin/login, wrong password shows admin-login-error, valid pupu/pupu2026 logs in and renders admin-dashboard with real stats (98 servers, 28,426 users, 0 in voice, 0 playing, 49ms latency), search filter narrows to 0 with no-match query, voice-only filter toggles, logout clears localStorage token and returns to login, and public status page still loads.
critical_code_review_comments: ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH is generated at process start with bcrypt.gensalt() rather than persisted — acceptable for a single-admin env-var setup, but every worker/restart yields a fresh salt (no login persistence issue since checkpw uses embedded salt, so OK).
login_attempts lockout keyed by ip+username: OK. Consider capping stored count and auto-expiring stale records via TTL index.

admin_control waits up to ~6s via a 15x0.4s poll loop — fine, but could use Motor change streams or an asyncio.Event for lower latency. Current behavior is correct and returns {ok:false,result:'no_player'} within ~2s as expected.

CORS: allow_credentials=True with allow_origins='*' from .env would be invalid per spec; currently CORS_ORIGINS='*' — since admin uses Bearer (not cookies), this is functionally OK but worth tightening for defense in depth.
pupu_bot.py is 1069 lines — consider splitting (commands, voice/wavelink handlers, status pusher) for maintainability.
test_credentials: admin username 'pupu' / password 'pupu2026' — verified from /app/memory/test_credentials.md and backend/.env
seed_data_creation: None. Used live bot status data pushed by pupu_bot (98 guilds).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Admin dashboard is fully working. Backend regression suite at /app/backend/tests/test_admin_api.py (13 tests). Bot is currently not in any voice channel, so control actions return {ok:false,result:'no_player'} — this is the intended, tested behavior. If future testing requires an active player, a voice-connected guild would be needed (out of automation scope).
